problem.name: PAC learning in the large-error regime
problem.name_latex: PAC learning in the large-error regime
problem.statement_latex: For a constructive $\lambda(n)$ satisfying $n^{\omega(1)}2^{-n/2}\le\lambda(n)\le n^{-\omega(1)}$, learn the concept class constructed by Oliveira from uniform quantum examples: output a classical circuit agreeing with the target on at least $1/2+\lambda(n)$ of inputs with probability at least $1-n^{-k}$, for fixed $k$.
problem.statement_text: For a constructive $\lambda(n)$ satisfying $n^{\omega(1)}2^{-n/2}\le\lambda(n)\le n^{-\omega(1)}$, learn the concept class constructed by Oliveira from uniform quantum examples: output a classical circuit agreeing with the target on at least $1/2+\lambda(n)$ of inputs with probability at least $1-n^{-k}$, for fixed $k$.

hardware.description_latex: Each example occupies $n+1$ logical qubits. The algorithm additionally needs the indicated number of coherent examples and its measurement/postprocessing workspace; preparing these examples is part of the supplied-access model.
hardware.description_text: Each example occupies $n+1$ logical qubits. The algorithm additionally needs the indicated number of coherent examples and its measurement/postprocessing workspace; preparing these examples is part of the supplied-access model.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time and examples by correlation-biased sampling of quadratic hypotheses and boosting. The general learner using $m$ examples achieves advantage $\Omega(\sqrt{m/2^n})$, failure $O(1/m)$ and time $m\operatorname{poly}(n)$.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time and examples by correlation-biased sampling of quadratic hypotheses and boosting. The general learner using $m$ examples achieves advantage $\Omega(\sqrt{m/2^n})$, failure $O(1/m)$ and time $m\operatorname{poly}(n)$.

classical.headline_latex: For the constructed class, no polynomial-time randomized membership-query learner attains even agreement $1/2+\lambda(n)/n^k$ with success above $n^{-k}$ on every target. Querying the complete effective truth table uses $O(n^{3k}\lambda(n)^{-2})$ queries up to polynomial factors from the construction.
classical.headline_text: For the constructed class, no polynomial-time randomized membership-query learner attains even agreement $1/2+\lambda(n)/n^k$ with success above $n^{-k}$ on every target. Querying the complete effective truth table uses $O(n^{3k}\lambda(n)^{-2})$ queries up to polynomial factors from the construction.
